entries.summary: In-game carbon-credit currency awarded for sequestration / efficient reactions.
entries.body:
## MOLCO2

MOLCO2 is the carbon-credit currency in molgang. Players earn MOLCO2 by:

- Running reactions that consume more CO₂ than they emit
- Building facilities with high atom economy
- Completing sustainability quests

MOLCO2 is spent on: facility upgrades that reduce emissions, license carbon-offset partnerships, and the marketplace.

See also: [atom-economy](#atom-economy), [carbon-credit](#carbon-credit).
entries.author: Vice

entries.summary: Effective partial pressure of a real gas — replaces ideal-gas pressure in chemical-equilibrium expressions.
entries.body:
## Fugacity

Fugacity (φ·P) is the *effective* partial pressure of a real gas. It substitutes for raw pressure in Gibbs free-energy / equilibrium-constant expressions when the gas deviates from ideal behavior.

- For an ideal gas: fugacity = pressure.
- For a real gas at high P or low T: fugacity ≠ pressure; fugacity coefficient φ < 1 means attractive interactions dominate.

In molgang, the in-game reactor sim tracks fugacity for any reaction running above ~10 bar.

See also: [activity](#activity), [chemical-potential](#chemical-potential).
entries.author: Kimi

entries.summary: Sum over all microstates weighted by Boltzmann factor — connects quantum energy levels to thermodynamic state functions.
entries.body:
## Partition function (Q)

The partition function Q = Σ exp(−Eᵢ/kT) sums Boltzmann-weighted microstates. Every macroscopic thermodynamic quantity (Helmholtz free energy, entropy, heat capacity) follows from Q.

In molgang the reaction simulator computes Q for translational + rotational + vibrational + electronic modes and uses it to predict equilibrium constants from first principles.

See also: [boltzmann-distribution](#boltzmann-distribution), [vibrational-mode](#vibrational-mode).
entries.author: Kimi

entries.summary: Dimensionless ratio of reaction rate to transport rate — tells you whether kinetics or mixing limits a reactor.
entries.body:
## Damköhler number

Da = (reaction rate) / (transport rate). Roughly:

- Da ≪ 1 → reactor is *transport-limited*; molecules leave before reacting.
- Da ≫ 1 → reactor is *kinetics-limited*; reaction equilibrates faster than flow / diffusion can supply reactants.

In molgang facility design, Da is the headline number on every continuous-flow reactor card.

See also: [residence-time](#residence-time), [péclet-number](#peclet-number).
entries.author: Kimi

entries.summary: Player-progression tiers (8-10, 11-13, 14-17, 18+) gating quests, mechanics, and chemistry depth.
entries.body:
## Age bands

molgang quests + mechanics are gated by four age bands so the game scales from middle-school casual to undergraduate-curriculum:

- **8-10**: ion-pair matching, simple reactions, no thermodynamics math.
- **11-13**: balancing equations, intro stoichiometry, MOLCO2 trading.
- **14-17**: thermodynamics + kinetics, real-gas corrections, full reactor design.
- **18+**: quantum chemistry path, partition functions, transport phenomena.

Age band is set in the player profile and gates every quest unlock.
entries.author: Vice

entries.summary: Green-chemistry metric measuring the fraction of reactant atoms that end up in the desired product rather than waste.
entries.body:
## Atom economy

Atom economy, introduced by Barry Trost, compares the molecular weight of the desired product to the total molecular weight of all reactants. A high atom economy means fewer by-products and less environmental waste.

In molgang, every synthesis quest displays an atom-economy score. Players earn bonus MOLCO2 when they design routes that exceed 80 % atom economy, encouraging greener choices such as catalytic hydrogenation over stoichiometric reductions.

Improving atom economy often requires unlocking advanced catalysts or switching to one-pot syntheses. The metric appears on the reaction summary card alongside yield and energy cost.

See also: [molco2](#molco2), [carbon-credit](#carbon-credit).
entries.author: Kimi

entries.summary: Tradeable permit representing the right to emit one tonne of CO₂ equivalent, earned by operating below emissions caps.
entries.body:
## Carbon credit

A carbon credit is a tradeable certificate granting the holder the right to emit one tonne of CO₂ equivalent. In molgang, credits are earned by operating below a facility's emissions cap and can be sold on the marketplace or retired for reputation gains.

Players can also invest in offset projects—reforestation modules or direct-air-capture rigs—to generate additional credits. The in-game carbon market fluctuates based on server-wide emissions, creating a player-driven economy around sustainability.

Managing credits is essential for high-tier reactor licenses. Running carbon-negative processes yields surplus credits that form a steady revenue stream for veteran players.

See also: [molco2](#molco2), [atom-economy](#atom-economy).
entries.author: Kimi

entries.summary: Structured missions that guide player progression through synthesis, engineering, and sustainability challenges.
entries.body:
## Quests

Quests are the primary progression mechanism in molgang. Each quest presents a specific chemistry or engineering challenge—synthesize a target molecule, minimize energy use, or scale a reaction to pilot-plant size.

Quests are gated by age band and faction reputation. Completing a quest rewards MOLCO2, experience, and occasionally unique catalyst blueprints. Daily and weekly quests rotate through the community board, encouraging replayability and collaborative competition.

Advanced quest lines culminate in capstone projects that require designing an entire process flowsheet. Successful completion unlocks the next age band and expands the player's facility build limit.

See also: [age-bands](#age-bands), [molco2](#molco2).
entries.author: Kimi

entries.summary: Partial molar Gibbs free energy — the thermodynamic force that drives matter to flow between phases or react.
entries.body:
## Chemical potential

The chemical potential μᵢ is the partial molar Gibbs free energy of component *i* in a mixture. It quantifies how the total free energy changes when an infinitesimal amount of *i* is added, holding temperature, pressure, and all other amounts constant.

Chemical potential is the true driving force for phase equilibrium, diffusion, and chemical reaction. When μᵢ is equal in two phases, net transfer stops; when reactants have a higher total chemical potential than products, the reaction proceeds spontaneously.

In molgang, the simulator uses chemical potentials derived from partition functions to compute equilibrium compositions without relying on empirical equilibrium constants.

See also: [fugacity](#fugacity), [partition-function](#partition-function).
entries.author: Kimi

entries.summary: Average duration a fluid element spends inside a reactor — the inverse of space velocity.
entries.body:
## Residence time

Residence time τ is the average period a fluid element remains inside a reactor, defined as reactor volume divided by volumetric flow rate (τ = V / Q). It is the inverse of space velocity and sets the temporal scale against which reaction rates are compared.

Short residence times favor fast reactions or high throughput; long residence times allow slow equilibria to approach completion. Together with the Damköhler number, τ reveals whether a reactor is limited by kinetics or by flow.

In molgang, players adjust residence time by changing reactor volume or pump speed. The tooltip shows the resulting conversion for the current reaction mechanism.

See also: [damkohler](#damkohler), [mass-transfer](#mass-transfer).
entries.author: Kimi

entries.summary: Probability distribution giving the relative populations of quantum states as an exponential function of their energy and temperature.
entries.body:
## Boltzmann distribution

The Boltzmann distribution states that the probability of finding a system in a quantum state *i* with energy Eᵢ is proportional to exp(−Eᵢ / kT). At higher temperatures, more excited states become populated; as T approaches zero, only the ground state remains occupied.

This distribution is the statistical-mechanical foundation of the partition function. From it, molgang's simulator computes internal energy, entropy, and equilibrium constants for reactions involving vibrational and electronic excitations.

Players rarely edit the distribution directly, but it underlies every temperature-dependent rate constant shown in the kinetics panel. Understanding it explains why some reactions accelerate dramatically with heat while others plateau.

See also: [partition-function](#partition-function).
entries.author: Kimi

entries.summary: Quantum-mechanical mixing of atomic orbitals to form equivalent hybrid orbitals that determine molecular geometry.
entries.body:
## Hybridization

Hybridization is the quantum-mechanical combination of atomic orbitals on a central atom to produce a set of equivalent hybrid orbitals. Common schemes include sp (linear), sp² (trigonal planar), and sp³ (tetrahedral), each dictating bond angles and thereby molecular shape.

In molgang, the molecule builder visually highlights hybridized lobes when players place atoms. Correct hybridization affects steric strain energy and reaction accessibility—an sp² carbon in a double bond, for example, cannot rotate freely like an sp³ single bond.

Understanding hybridization helps players predict nucleophilic attack angles and design catalysts with optimal orbital overlap for transition-state stabilization.
entries.author: Kimi

entries.summary: Transport of species across concentration gradients — the physical movement that brings reactants together and removes products.
entries.body:
## Mass transfer

Mass transfer is the net movement of species from regions of high concentration to low concentration, driven by diffusion, convection, or both. In chemical engineering, it encompasses external transfer across boundary layers and internal transfer within porous catalyst pellets.

High mass-transfer rates ensure reactants reach active sites and products escape, preventing equilibrium limitations. When mass transfer is slower than intrinsic kinetics, the observed reaction rate drops and the reactor behaves as if governed by a smaller rate constant.

In molgang, players upgrade agitators, packing material, and membrane separators to boost mass-transfer coefficients. The facility card shows whether the current step is reaction-controlled or transfer-controlled.

See also: [residence-time](#residence-time), [damkohler](#damkohler).
